status: PROPOSAL — staged. Erik: 'a player becomes both a target, and can be sent on a strike mission... or to guard someone under threat.'
whyThisIsTheKeystone: Until now the world sim has been a very good machine the player WATCHES. Arcs move, legends die, vacancies open — and none of it asks anything of them. THE THIRD ACTION CHANGES THAT, because a strike is the first world event that has a SINGLE NAMED TARGET AND A DEADLINE. That is a quest. ⚠️ SO THE WORLD SIM STOPS BEING BACKGROUND AND STARTS BEING THE QUEST GENERATOR — and the quests are not authored, they are TRUE: the target really is the most valuable worker on that arc, and the arc really does move if they die.

thePiecesAlreadyExist.ws.arcCasualties: who was hurt or killed over an arc this pass — CCODE-117
thePiecesAlreadyExist.ws.arcContests: who won and by how much
thePiecesAlreadyExist.startStructuredQuest(character, def, ctx: takes a def object — a generated def is as valid as an authored one
thePiecesAlreadyExist.the news block: worldtick.js:1201 already assembles rumors NPCs might repeat
thePiecesAlreadyExist.verdict: ⚠️ NOTHING NEW IS NEEDED TO CARRY THIS. The sim knows who is valuable, who is hated, who is exposed, and who just died. The quest is a projection of state that already exists.

theThreeRoles.trigger: the party is holding an arc position AND a hostile striker's disposition fires against them
theThreeRoles.whoComesFor_you: ⚠️ DERIVED, NOT ROLLED. The Quiet Work comes for the party's HIGHEST-WEIGHT contributor — the one actually moving the arc. The Crusade comes for whoever's arc-position most offends the crusader, which may be a lesser member. THOSE ARE DIFFERENT SCENES: one is an assassin in the night after your best; the other is a declared campaign against the person whose position they cannot bear.
theThreeRoles.theWarning: a crusade is DECLARED, so the party gets notice. A quiet strike gives none — unless a verist, a Foresense craft, or a bought rumor reveals it. ⚠️ THAT IS AN ENORMOUS ARGUMENT FOR INFORMATION AS A PURCHASABLE GOOD, and the economy already supports it.
theThreeRoles.thestakes: a party that parks a healer safely behind the line is EXACTLY the back-line target this system models. Being safe is now a position, not a guarantee.

theThreeRoles.trigger: a faction/legend aligned with the party needs a worker removed and cannot reach them
theThreeRoles.targetSelection: the same rule the NPC strikers use — the most valuable enemy worker on a contested arc. ⚠️ SO THE QUEST IS HONEST: they are asking the player to kill the person who is genuinely holding that arc, and the arc will genuinely move.
theThreeRoles.themoralWeight: ⚠️ THE TARGET IS USUALLY NOT A VILLAIN. The most valuable worker on an arc is, statistically, a heroic-tier figure quietly tending something. Being sent to kill them is the single sharpest moral scene the world can generate, AND NOBODY HAS TO WRITE IT — it falls out of who is winning.
theThreeRoles.refusal: declining must be a real option with a real cost (standing with the asker), never a soft-lock.

theThreeRoles.role: GUARD — the player is asked to protect
theThreeRoles.trigger: an arc-critical worker on the party's side is a likely strike target (high weight, low engagement, unprotected)
theThreeRoles.whyItIsTheBestOfTheThree: It gives a party a reason to CARE ABOUT AN NPC THEY DID NOT CHOOSE. The world says 'she is the reason the Palelands still have medicine, and someone is coming for her.' That is a stake the game has never been able to generate before, and it is TRUE — she really is holding that arc.
theThreeRoles.theTension: guarding means STANDING STILL while other arcs move without you. The vacancy mechanic applies to the party too — protecting one front costs you the others.
theThreeRoles.failure: ⚠️ FAILURE MUST BE SURVIVABLE AND VISIBLE. If the guard fails, the worker dies, the arc moves, and the world says so by name. That is a loss the player can read in the world state afterward.

whatMakesTheseQuestsDifferentFromAUTHORE: THEY ARE TRUE. An authored quest asserts that the target matters; a generated one is drawn from a target who measurably IS moving the arc.

THEY EXPIRE. The window is the strike window. A quest to guard someone who has already been killed is not offered, and a quest to strike someone who already died is withdrawn — which the sim state supports directly.
THEY DIFFER PER WORLD. The arcs already diverge across seeds; so the same campaign generates different missions in different worlds, against different people.
AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS MEASURABLE. The player can look at the arc afterward and see the number move. That is the payoff the whole world-sim chain has been building toward.
designGuards: ⚠️ RATE-LIMIT HARD. A strike is ~0.08 per pass across the whole world; player-facing strike quests should be RARER still — a handful per campaign, not a repeatable. The moment this becomes a quest treadmill it stops being an event.

NEVER AUTO-RESOLVE A PLAYER STRIKE IN THE SIM. If the player is on the mission, the sim must WAIT for the play outcome rather than rolling it. A world that already killed the target before the party arrives is the worst version of this.

THE ASKER MUST BE SOMEONE. A faceless 'the Orders want this done' wastes the mechanic. It should be a named legend whose want the player can read — and whose want explains why they cannot go themselves.

AND GUARD QUESTS SHOULD SOMETIMES BE UNWINNABLE-BY-FORCE: the striker who cannot be beaten in a fight but can be DETECTED, deterred, or out-waited. That is what the stillhold and umbral crafts are for, and it stops guard duty from being a combat encounter with extra steps.
openForErik: Should the party be able to be RECRUITED BY THE OTHER SIDE? A crusader asking the party to help destroy a worker they have previously guarded is the sharpest version of this system, and it needs no new machinery.

Does a successful player strike promote the ASKER? Under promotion-by-duration, removing a rival's key worker helps the asker's arc — so a player can make a legend. THAT WOULD BE A REMARKABLE THING TO BE ABLE TO SAY.

How much warning for a quiet strike against the player? My read: NONE by default, and information becomes something you buy, cultivate, or craft for. It makes verists, foresense crafts and rumor-brokers matter enormously.
